final_candidates.decision_summary: Thr-to-Ile in the HA1 body removes a polar hydroxyl in favor of a hydrophobic side chain, a commonly stabilizing substitution pattern away from receptor-binding residues. Low expected impact on cell entry.
Asn-to-Asp near the head/trimer interface may enable new salt-bridge pairing, plausibly increasing trimer thermostability. Some risk of altered surface chemistry near glycosylation-adjacent regions.
Conservative polar-to-hydrophobic change in a surface loop that reduces solvent-entropy cost of folding with minimal entry risk. Expected stability gain is modest.

stop_reason.detail: No external evidence is available and further self-iteration is unlikely to change the Top-3 ranking.

history.rationale: Position 318 (HA numbering; T in 'TSTLNQ' region near receptor-binding site periphery) — Thr-to-Ile stabilizes hydrophobic packing in the head domain without altering receptor-binding residues, a common stabilizing substitution in HA thermostability engineering.
Thr-to-Ile removes a polar hydroxyl in the HA1 body, a common stabilizing substitution pattern in group-1/HA stem-adjacent regions without altering receptor-binding residues.

Replacing an Asn near the 320-loop reduces local flexibility and removes a potential deamidation site; acidic residue formation of stabilizing salt bridges in HA head domain has been reported to raise thermal tolerance.

Position 330 sits in HA1 head near the trimer interface; N-to-D may improve salt-bridge pairing but risks changing glycosylation-adjacent surface chemistry, so confidence slightly lowered pending structure-based reasoning.
HA1 Thr156 near a glycosylation-adjacent loop; Thr→Ala is small and mildly helix-stabilizing; documented that HA1 loop rigidification improves heat stability without affecting receptor binding.
Conservative polar-to-hydrophobic substitution in a surface loop; removing Thr OH reduces solvent-entropy cost but is away from known folding nuclei, so impact is modest.
Introducing Pro at a loop position in HA1 could rigidify a flexible loop; however, Pro can also destabilize helices so this is lower confidence pending structural considerations.
Proline insertion into a β-strand/loop region (site 123 lies in the vestigial esterase subdomain) is more likely to disrupt local structure than stabilize it.

rejection.reason: Proline insertion into a β-strand/loop region (site 123 lies in the vestigial esterase subdomain) is more likely to disrupt local structure than stabilize it.

history.rationale: Conservative Asp→Glu retains charge while improving side-chain packing/salt-bridge geometry near the 220-loop; low risk to receptor binding (position 225 is adjacent to, not within, key RBS contacts).

Adding a consensus-adjacent glycosylation-adjacent Asn-type residue near the 220 loop; changes in this loop are risky for receptor specificity so this is a moderate-confidence candidate for stability via local consensus restoration.
223 is immediately adjacent to the receptor-binding 220-loop; adding a bulky N-linked-glycosylation-competent Asn near RBS is high risk for cell entry.

rejection.reason: 223 is immediately adjacent to the receptor-binding 220-loop; adding a bulky N-linked-glycosylation-competent Asn near RBS is high risk for cell entry.

Conservative acidic residue shortening; plausible small helix-stabilizing effect with minimal entry risk.

C-terminal HA2 position; adding a hydrophobic residue at the transmembrane-adjacent region could enhance membrane-proximal stability, but functional risk near the TM domain warrants moderate-low confidence.
